newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-W.P. TAKE ON GRIQUAS IN KEY CLASH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-W.P. TAKE ON GRIQUAS IN KEY CLASH.

text.p: Griqualand West may be missing influential playmaker Boeta Wessels at fullback for their important Currie Cup showdown with Western Province at Newlands on Saturday, but the visitors will still fancy their chances of retainng third place on the section B table.

Wessels has missed Griquas' last few matches through injury but, with the more important quarter-final to come, his province have decided not to risk him for a key clash in Cape Town which will determine third and fourth spots in the section.
Whichever of the two side loses in Cape Town on Saturday will play their quarter-final match against defending Currie Cup champions Natal in Durban on October 12.

Despite an inferior points record to Western Province, Griqualand West have played the better rugby this season when it has mattered. Griquas enjoy seven wins and a draw last weekend with Free State from their 11 section outings and they lie one point ahead of W.P. on the table with 15 points.

They have proved to be a difficult side to beat at home this year -- drawing impressively with Taine Randell's mid-week All Blacks to prove the point -- and are well-balanced in all departments of the game.
But on Saturday they face a Western Province line-up keen to make up for an erratic, and largely disappointing, season.

On this occasion, Province will be enjoying home advantage and they have made only one change to the side which demolished South-Western Districts in Mossel Bay last weekend. Utility forward FC Smit returns from injury for Nico Wegner.
Both W.P. and Griquas possess backs who are both talented and youthful and, given suitable weather conditions, expansive rugby could result once the respective packs have tested each other out.
With Natal and Northern Transvaal having completely dominated their sections this season, Saturday's other Currie Cup matches look fairly predictable on paper.

Eastern Province, who have not enjoyed the best of fortune this year, should win comfortably away against bottom-placed Western Transvaal in Potchefstroom while Border will simply be hoping for damage limitation in their match against impressive Natal
In Wellington, Boland, lying fourth in section A, take on a Transvaal side which finally seems to be producing the rugby of which their wealth of Springboks should be capable.

On Friday night, top-of-the-table Northern Transvaal should annihilate South-Western Districts at Loftus Versfeld while Free State should have few problems entertaining Northern Free State in Bloemfontein.
